# Tool reference: SimCity 4 server (simcity4)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's tools/list; do not edit by hand -->

16 tools. Every tool takes JSON arguments as described and returns compact JSON text, except `guide` (markdown). Failures are MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) whose text is JSON `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}`.

Kinds map to the MCP tool annotations each tool carries:

| kind | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| read | True | False | True | reads the game, changes nothing |
| act | False | False | False | acts in the game |
| destructive | False | True | False | can discard or destroy something (unsaved city, a file, the game process) |

All tools have openWorldHint false (they act on the local game only).

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization:

> Tools for playing SimCity 4 Deluxe (1.1.641) through the game's own code. Start with guide(), then game_launch(). Coordinates are city cells; regions are grids of city tiles. Every result is JSON; failures are tool errors with {error, hint}.

## guide

*read*

How to use this server: the guide for agents, by topic.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string | `'start'` | "start" (overview and first steps), "all" (the whole guide) or a section name such as "regions". |

## game_launch

*act*

Start SimCity 4 (or attach to the instance SiMCP started earlier) and connect to it. The game runs without administrator rights and with SiMCP's own user folder (its own Regions and settings; the player's plugins are mirrored, so the simulation is the same), and opens on the region view. Returns the game status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `windowed` | boolean | `true` | run in a window (true) or full screen. |
| `width` | integer | `1024` | window / screen width in pixels (screen recipes are measured at 1024x768). |
| `height` | integer | `768` | window / screen height in pixels. |
| `intro` | boolean | `false` | play the intro movie. |
| `timeout_s` | integer | `120` | seconds to wait for the game to finish starting. |

## game_status

*read*

Whether SimCity 4 is running and controllable, and what it shows (region view or a city).

No parameters.

## list_regions

*read*

The regions in SiMCP's user folder with their city tiles (grid position, size small / medium / large) and each tile's saved city (name, mayor, established or not, populations). Reads files: works without the game.

No parameters.

## load_region

*act*

Open a region in the region view (the game's own LoadRegion). Works from the region view; leave a city first.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | the region's folder name as list_regions shows it (e.g. "MCP Test", "Timbuktu"). |

## load_city

*act*

Open a city of the loaded region with the region view's own LoadCity: with a name, the founded city of that name; without one, the first unfounded tile of the given size (it opens in god mode: terrain only). Returns the city's status.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `''` | a founded city's name as list_regions shows it, or "" for an unfounded tile. |
| `size` | string | `'any'` | for an unfounded tile: "small" (64x64 cells), "medium" (128x128), "large" (256x256) or "any". |

## leave_city

*destructive*

Go back to the region view without saving (unsaved changes to the city are lost).

No parameters.

## advance_time

*act*

Advance the open city by exactly this many game days, far faster than real time, with the game's own day code: every day runs all of the simulation's daily, weekly, monthly and yearly work. The game's own pause and speed settings are left as they were. Returns the new date; if max_seconds runs out first, remaining_days says how many days are left (call again to continue).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | `1` | game days to advance (1 or more). |
| `max_seconds` | number | `60.0` | wall-clock limit for this call (keep it under your client's tool timeout). |

## city_status

*read*

The open city: name, mayor, founded or not, difficulty, size in cells, the game date, speed and pause state. Read from the game's memory.

No parameters.

## map_data

*read*

One data layer of the open city as a grid, read from the game's memory: the values the game's data views and simulation use. Call with no layer to list the layers. Values are per tract (tract_size cells square; rows[z][x] in tract units); a cell (x, z) is in tract (x // tract_size, z // tract_size).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | `''` | a layer name ("zones", "land_value", "crime", "police_coverage", "fire_coverage", "air_pollution", "water_pollution", "garbage", "power", "water", "traffic_congestion", "mayor_rating", ...); "" lists them. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | first cell column of the area to return (0 = west edge). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | first cell row of the area to return. |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | last cell column (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | last cell row (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |

## tile_info

*read*

Everything about one cell of the open city: the value of every data layer there, the terrain altitude at its corners, water depth and sea level, and the lot / building standing on it. Read from memory.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | cell column (0 = west edge). |
| `z` | integer | required | cell row (0 = north edge). |

## get_budget

*read*

The city's money: funds, the tax rate of every zone and wealth group, this month's income and expenses, last month's, year to date, the game's end-of-year estimate, and loans. Read from the game.

No parameters.

## demand

*read*

Residential, commercial and industrial demand per wealth group, as the game's demand graph shows it, with the share blocked by caps, plus the number of residents.

No parameters.

## lots

*read*

The lots of the open city with their building: position, size, facing, zone, wealth, state (occupied, abandoned, under construction...), historical, power, and the building's name and exemplar id.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string | `''` | only lots of this zone (e.g. "residential_low", "industrial_high", "plopped"); "" = all. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | west edge of the area (cells). |
| `z0` | integer | `0` | north edge of the area (cells). |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | east edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `z1` | integer | `-1` | south edge (inclusive; -1 = the city's edge). |
| `limit` | integer | `500` | at most this many lots in the answer (count always gives the total). |

## advisors

*read*

What the city's advisors say now: each advisor's mood and current messages (title, mood, priority, text) - the same advice the game shows in its advisor panel, popups and news ticker.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_fluff` | boolean | `false` | also list the fluffy news (jokes without game meaning). |

## quit_game

*destructive*

Quit SimCity 4 without saving (an open city's unsaved changes are lost; save first if needed).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | `false` | end the process instead of asking the game to quit (use only if the game no longer responds). |
